**#330 hit live: .memory JSONL auto-merges CLEAN with no markers — git never warns, so silent record loss is the real risk**

**What**: #330 (`.memory/index.jsonl` has no merge strategy) materialized for real on 2026-07-25, right after #333 merged to main and PR #338 was left behind. Concrete evidence for raising its priority.

**The non-obvious part — the danger is NOT a conflict**: `git merge origin/main` reported `Auto-merging .memory/index.jsonl` / `Auto-merging .memory/records/2026-07.jsonl` / `Auto-merging .memory/manifest.json` and **"Automatic merge went well"**. Zero conflict markers. GitHub had reported the PR as CONFLICTING, but locally git resolved it silently.

That is the failure mode. A line-based auto-merge of append-only JSONL can drop or interleave records and git will never say a word. Nobody reviews a file git called clean.

**How it was verified (do this every time)**: do not trust the clean merge. Compare by SET of `sync_id`:
```
claves únicas   main: 1487   mine: 1490   merged: 1490
LOST from main:  0
LOST from mine:  0
expected union:  1490  ✓
```
Result was correct — zero records lost either side. Mine was a strict superset of main's because both branches exported from the same engram DB. But correctness here was luck plus verification, not a guarantee from the tooling.

**Separate PRE-EXISTING finding, not caused by the merge**: `.memory/records/2026-07.jsonl` carries **89 duplicate `sync_id` entries**, present identically on BOTH sides (origin/main 1576 lines / 89 dups; branch 1579 / 89). So `memory:share` is re-exporting already-exported observations. Untouched — needs its own ticket. It is also pure bloat on exactly the file whose size caused #332 (the 1 MiB execFileSync ceiling).

**Where**: `.memory/index.jsonl`, `.memory/records/2026-07.jsonl`, `.memory/manifest.json`. Merge commit on `feature/335-epic-governance-m10-seam-contract-covera`.

**Why #330 should rise in priority**: with `csrinaldibot` now active on #317 plus parallel PRs, this is no longer theoretical. The next occurrence, with nobody comparing sets by hand, loses records silently — git will print "went well". A `merge=union` gitattributes driver (or a dedicated merge driver that dedups by `sync_id`) would make it deterministic and would also fix the 89-duplicate bloat.

**Learned**: GitHub's `mergeable` field is computed asynchronously and stays stale right after a push. It read `CONFLICTING` for a while after the merge was pushed, then flipped to `MERGEABLE`. Poll it rather than trusting the first read — the same read-a-verdict-against-changed-state shape as #328.</content>
</invoke>
